claims.explanation: PP-2 is a pyrazolopyrimidine Src-family kinase inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern tracks with dependence on Src/FAK signaling rather than any single lineage. Lines with activated RTK/RAS-PI3K signaling (KRAS, BRAF, PTEN loss, PIK3CA) and intact Src/FAK pathway components are most sensitive, while lines with alternative survival wiring (e.g., SMARCA4 loss, NF1/STK11 co-mutation, or low Src-family expression) are protected. The transcriptional similarity to PP-1 and PI3K/mTOR inhibitors supports a Src-to-PI3K/AKT mechanism of action.

features.basis: PP-2 is an SRC inhibitor; target expression predicts dependence
FAK/Src complex mediates survival signaling; PP-2 blocks FAK Y397/Y577 phosphorylation
RAS-driven lines (GSU_STOMACH, SNU81, LS1034, RERFLCAD1, MKN1) are enriched among sensitive lines
BRAF-mutant lines (HEC265, IGR37) appear among sensitive lines
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT downstream of Src; enriched in sensitive lines
PI3K pathway activation may increase dependence on Src-driven survival signaling
SMARCA4-mutant lines (COV434, PLCPRF5, FTC238) are enriched among least-affected lines
NF1-mutant lines (BICR6, PLCPRF5, COLO792, S117) appear among least-affected lines
STK11-mutant lines (G361, PLCPRF5, 22RV1) are enriched among least-affected lines
CDKN2A loss appears in several least-affected lines (ASPC1, HS939T, HEP3B217, SNU899)
ALK-altered lines (NCIH2452, G361) show reduced sensitivity
TP53 mutation is nearly universal in sensitive lines but also common in resistant lines, so weak evidence
